title: Announcing New Capabilities in Mastra Factory
summary: Build your software from issue to production, with app previews, Slack-native collaboration, and any models.
body_markdown:
Today, we're launching dramatic improvements to[Mastra Factory](https://factory.mastra.ai/) .


Mastra Factory is an open-source software factory that helps teams ship software faster and more consistently, built on the same Mastra building blocks you already know and love.


Your browser does not support the video tag.


We believe great products will be built by humans backed by strong delivery systems unique to each company. We aim for every part of that system to be customizable, swappable, and uniquely yours—just like the way **you** build software.


Since the[alpha](https://mastra.ai/blog/announcing-mastra-factory) launch in July and the[beta](https://mastra.ai/blog/announcing-mastra-factory-beta) in September, we've had hundreds of customer conversations and merged nearly 1000 PRs improving Factory. We've focused on performance, reliability, and novel capabilities that solve real customer pain points.


That said, in the age of AI, we care deeply about long-term commitments to stability, reliability, and software that *just works* . We're not yet launching Factory as a 1.0.0 release; we'll continue to evolve, improve, and harden it. The factory metaphor is intentional: we aim to deliver software you can use to build your software your way, consistently, predictably, and with the controls you choose and customize.


## What we're launching


Today we're launching new capabilities for a software factory you can set up, customize, and deploy to start doing real work in under five minutes. What you can expect:


- **Intake sources.** Factories need inputs, and inputs for software come from many sources: GitHub, Gitlab, Linear, Jira, or incidents from systems like Incident.io. All of these inputs shape what gets automated and built with the factory, and over time you can expect more intake sources available through[Mastra Connect](https://mastra.ai/docs/mastra-platform/connect) .
- **Customizable workflow stages.** Work progresses from intake to shipped through customizable workflow states like **Triage** , **Plan** , **Review** , and **Done** . Each stage is fully customizable with your own skill, tooling, and team preferences as it relates to guardrails and human approvals.
- **Coding agent.** We're launching with a cloud coding agent (backed by[Mastra Code](https://code.mastra.ai/) ) that includes our[state of the art observational memory](https://mastra.ai/research/observational-memory-beam) persisted across work items on the board.
- **Integrated workspaces.** Software is increasingly being generated in cloud environments that proxy your local environment as closely as possible. We bundle a microVM (we use E2B by default in Mastra platform) available to all sessions to do work as close as possible to your team's development environment and preferences.
- **Flexible connectors.** Sometimes factory work needs additional context from team tools outside of issue tracking and version control. Mastra Connect integrates with Factory to provide common connections your team needs to get work done.
- **Support for any model.** We support[any model provider](https://mastra.ai/models/providers) and gateway (including our[Mastra Gateway](https://mastra.ai/models/gateways/mastra) ), inference providers, frontier labs, and any OpenAI-compatible model shape.


## Get started


Getting started is just a prompt away with your favorite coding agent, or you can[read the documentation](https://factory.mastra.ai/) if that's more your jam.


Terminal


```text
Set up Mastra Factory for me. Ask me what to name my factory, then run npx create-factory <factory-name>. Next, run cd <factory-name> && npm run dev and open http://localhost:4111. Documentation: https://factory.mastra.ai
```


## New capabilities


We're also excited about new capabilities that have been an unlock for the Mastra team as we've used Factory to build our own software factories.


### Previews


**See it, then ship it.** Every change comes with a live preview link, so you click through the real app before you ever open the diff.


### Cloud sandboxes


**Off your laptop.** Every agent gets its own cloud sandbox, repos cloned and ready. Run ten in parallel and your fans never spin up.


### Slack-native


**Ship from the thread.** Mention Factory to file work, answer its questions, and approve plans without switching tabs.


### Infinite control and customization


**Yours, not ours.** Boards, stages, human-in-the-loop approvals (or not), and models are all customizable, swappable, and tweakable.


### App previews


For those in the know, you may recognize that much of the Mastra team's DNA was shaped and molded by building developer tools at Gatsby, Netlify, and other strong developer-centric products and cultures. One thing we learned is how important iteration velocity is for building great products, and so today we're excited to launch[app previews](https://factory.mastra.ai/using/previews) , which are ephemeral development environments that persist across work sessions in the factory. Other tools give you a simulacrum of "the app" with screenshots and code, but the reality is that more and more code is produced by teammates further and further away from it. The best thing to see and interact with is actually just the site itself, which dramatically improves iteration velocity and enables teams to be confident that things are working with a high degree of confidence.

### Slack-native user experience


In general, we aim to integrate with any collaborative channel ([Teams, WhatsApp, Discord](https://mastra.ai/integrations) , wherever you collaborate!), but in this release we focused primarily on ensuring a top-tier Slack-native experience. This seems easy but a heavily constrained service is an interesting design and engineering problem. Specifically, we have built in the following capabilities by default.


- **Ambient mode.** When your factory instance is tagged into a thread, it chooses to reply and judges whether or not it should reply. Think of it like a highly capable member of your team, not a simpleton assistant.
- **Signals.** Signals are an observability mechanism that has been missing from all harnesses and coding agents. Specifically,[Signals](https://mastra.ai/docs/signals/overview) is a Mastra primitive that is used to listen, observe, and steer the turn based on an upstream state change. To give a practical example, we leverage CodeRabbit for PR reviews and without any configuration the work item subscribes to the reviews and automatically addresses the comments.
- **Files and previews.** By default, the agent loop has appropriate tools to share context from the work in progress, whether that's screenshots, full app previews, or whether you share files (CSVs, JSON, Markdown, you name it) the agent loop ingests and updates its context / turn appropriately and then outputs data just like you expect.
- **Generative UI.** You can opt in to generative UI, which is a mode where the agent harness can choose to output rich, interactive Slack-native data structures like bar charts and pie charts.

### Cloud Workspaces


Local coding agents (like[Mastra Code](https://code.mastra.ai/) ) are game changers for engineers. But because they run locally, they come with limitations and frustrations, like managing worktrees and kicking off and managing multiple threads. They're also limited by bottlenecks inherent in single-player development.


We are launching with support for customizable sandbox environments that persist across sessions. We fully support:


- **Docker.** Customize the Docker image that gets deployed with the sandbox.
- **Memory and CPU.** Customize the desired memory and CPU based upon the compute consumption of your project(s).
- **Persistent, stable URLs.** As mentioned earlier, App Previews are a flagship feature unlocked with our Cloud Workspaces that just work for improving iteration velocity.


In essence, our aim and ambition is that you can ship *your local* to *our sandbox* environments and enable your team to be highly effective and productive regardless of proximity to their machine.


### Model flexibility and failover


Just like with Mastra, we aim for guiding principles of control and customization. This means that teams can come with a gateway, inference provider, or preferred model family of their choice and fully control how these models are used in the factory instance. We support three modes:


- **Personal.** Every model run defaults to the model preferences of the user who originated the session.
- **Hybrid.** Work items (the "board") default to org-level models, and user sessions can be customized per user.
- **Org.** The board and sessions default to org-chosen and enforced model families.


We fully integrate any inference provider that is OpenAI compatible (OpenRouter, Ramp Router, etc.), frontier and open-weight models, and of course our own,[Mastra Gateway](https://mastra.ai/models/gateways/mastra) . We also support[custom model gateways](https://mastra.ai/models/gateways/custom-gateways) for cases where data privacy and compliance restrictions apply.


Models, intelligence, and cost are key factors in the success of AI adoption in your company and reflect your unique preferences. We aim to meet you exactly where you are to help you build your software factory.


## How we use Mastra Factory at Mastra


Factory claims deserve skepticism. The loudest claims tend to come from teams with dramatic shipping stories and almost no users. So instead of claiming, here's how the Mastra team has used our own factory, which we call "Shipyard", and what it measurably changed.


### First, the results


So with that mindset, these are the real, measurable improvements we've seen as a team using Mastra. We haven't artificially juiced the numbers, and we don't think we're done: we expect to embrace factories further and use them more. The reality is that no matter how good the tool, engineering remains a tool-assisted craft, where we stay conscious of what goes in, the effect of what goes in, and how to keep updating our systematic way of delivery to improve our product. So no, we won't be announcing today that engineers at Mastra are opening 1000 PRs per week, because they don't want that, users don't want that, and no one benefits except model labs.


So instead we're sharing the raw, transparent results we've seen as a team using Mastra. Substance, not hype.


### Human output


Before Factory, a Mastra engineer merged 9.5 PRs a week. Over the last four complete weeks, that number is 16.9, a **78%** increase.

### Adoption


In Beta, Factory was interesting but not consistently and uniformly trusted. A handful of power users on the Mastra team accounted for most of the usage, not unlike some of the early adoption of a tool like Claude Code at Anthropic, and numerous sharp edges were hindering adoption. Through early October, no more than three engineers ran Factory sessions in a given week. In each of the last three complete weeks, 19–24 engineers ran Factory sessions.

### What earned our trust


But perhaps more important than the results themselves is, you guessed it, the way we collaborate. Systematic control of inputs and outputs has led us to produce better software and to iterate on it more quickly and effectively. A few specific improvements we shipped built that trust:


- **Private by default.** As familiarity and trust was being earned, some engineers preferred to work in private UI-based sessions, which can be optionally shared with the organization. Over time, more and more of the team moved into our #shipyard-graveyard public channel to build, ship, and iterate in the open.
- **One kind of session.** In Beta, Factory had several different kinds of work streams, including a "supervisor" that had context from user sessions and work sessions. Our engineers didn't want to learn Shipyard's UI; they wanted Factory from wherever they were already working, whether that was[Mastra Code](https://code.mastra.ai/) or Slack. So we unified the model: any session has the tools to interact with the board, kick off user sessions, and thread context back. That leaves a single concept for a team member to learn, and it's one they already know: natural language!
- **Collaborative in Slack.** We don't necessarily aim to be the collaborative surface, we aim to integrate with the ones your team already uses. It feels a little unnatural to begin with shipping code from Slack, but we've seen a dramatic increase in this type of development. As code becomes more of a commodity, Slack is where we still level-up together, share context, and keep growing the engineering team at Mastra.


## What's next


We believe that Mastra Factory is a glimpse into how software is being built by the best teams in the world and how incorporating it into your processes will help accelerate and standardize your unique way of building software. To get closer to teams, we're offering early access and a unique ability to help shape the roadmap with our[Custom Factory program](https://mastra.ai/blog/introducing-custom-factory-program) , where you'll get direct exposure to the Mastra Factory roadmap and perhaps more importantly the Mastra team and forward deployed engineers to help you build your factory.


Keep building the future - we'll see you there ✌️


The Mastra Team
